run_note: Tuesday 2026-08-18, 10:15Z, before the US open. NO R1 BREACH AND NO SIM-INTEGRITY ALERT. THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE FLEET-WIDE FREEZE IS OVER: the loop restarted 2026-08-17T18:06:54Z after 5h49m dark (12:18Z to 18:06Z) and has run clean since. Every bot's state age now clusters at 11.6-11.8 minutes against a 13.4-minute cadence, the tightest reading in a week, and the real marking cadence over the last 24h has a MEDIAN gap of 13.5 minutes and a MAXIMUM non-freeze gap of 14.7 minutes. That last number matters because the raw GitHub run-start arithmetic looks alarming and is misleading: the largest interval between run STARTS in 24h is 105.7 minutes (08-18 00:00Z to 01:46Z) and 107 of 120 runs show 'cancelled'. Both are artifacts of the long-running-loop design, where each scheduled run cancels the previous one that is still cycling. I checked the thing that actually matters, the commit cadence on data/*_state.json, and there is no hole. I am NOT reporting a cron gap today. One workflow failure exists in the window, 2026-08-15T06:53:35Z, outside 24h and not recurring. WHAT THE RESTART COST: in the first cycle back, four books acted simultaneously and one of them detonated. sentiment bought NLST all-in at 6.51 within one second of the restart on a 'patent settlement buzz' tag, and its own -10% stop cut it 41 minutes later at 5.81 for -145.63, an 11% loss on the fleet's largest book, chasing a Samsung settlement that was announced twelve days earlier on 2026-08-05 and had already tripled the stock. NLST then closed 6.03, above the exit, so the stop sold near the low as well. That single trade is most of the fleet's day. FILL AUDIT NON-VACUOUS AND PASSING: nine new fills, all verified. The four equity legs (sentiment NLST buy 18:06:54Z and sell 18:47:25Z, hunter PLTR sell and SLV buy both 18:06:54Z) land at 14:06-14:47 ET, inside US regular hours, at prices inside their 08-17 ranges. The five crypto fills (hypecrypto GPS buy; lottery CHIP round trip, EDEN round trip, GPS buy) all sit inside Binance mainnet 1-minute ranges within +/-5 minutes of their timestamps. No market-hours breach, no out-of-range price. TWO BOTS CAME BACK FROM THE DEAD AND BOTH TRADED: hypecrypto, frozen 48 hours on the Binance 451 fault, took the first trade of its life at 18:06:54Z and is the fleet's third-best book at 1062.65; the Watcher's cadence is back to 1.8 hours against a 2-hour design. NEW FAULT THIS RUN, and it is a reasoning fault, not an outage: the Analyst's own guardrail tagged its 08-17 decision 'UNRECEIPTED WATCHER CLAIM (read_watcher not called)' - it asserted the Watcher's risk level in its stated reasoning without calling the tool that returns it - and in the same decision it labelled an intraday print as a close for the second time (quoted 'SPY closed 773.55 on 8/17'; the close was 772.67). MY OWN SCORING: one closure, my largest win to date, +145.64, and it was a stay-in-cash call on the hype book, which is now 8-0 on that exact call while my hype price views sit at 2W/8L. I am not treating that as skill at picking hype stocks; it is a single repeated observation that this strategy loses money when it acts.

open_faults.fault: fleet-wide freeze (12:18Z-18:06Z on 08-17) — RESOLVED, structural exposure unfixed
open_faults.status: RESOLVED this run; root cause still present in bot.yml
open_faults.detail: The loop restarted 2026-08-17T18:06:54Z after 5h49m dark and has cycled cleanly for 16 hours since: median state-commit gap 13.5 minutes, maximum 14.7 minutes, all eleven bots within 0.2 minutes of each other on age. The outage is over. What is NOT fixed is the exposure that produced it: .github/workflows/bot.yml iterates the bots serially with no per-bot timeout and no watchdog, so one network call that never returns freezes the whole fleet silently while the run stays green. It cost 5h49m and, because the restart dumped four bots into the market in one cycle 20 minutes before the close, it is also the proximate setting for the day's 145.63 loss. Owner's call; I do not touch workflows.

open_faults.fault: Analyst asserts Watcher readings it never fetched
open_faults.status: NEW this run — caught by the bot's own guardrail, not by me
open_faults.detail: guardrail_tag on the 2026-08-17 decision: 'agent decision - UNRECEIPTED WATCHER CLAIM (read_watcher not called)'. The decision text states 'Watcher is caution, not SEVERE' and lists three of its items, but tools_called is ['get_price_history'] only. The claim happened to be correct, which is worse rather than better: an agent that reproduces a plausible risk reading from memory will eventually reproduce a stale one and act on it. Its third pre-committed trigger is 'Watcher SEVERE -> immediate exit to CASH', so this is the exact input its own falsifier depends on. Credit where due: the guardrail caught this and stamped it.
